fluff.overview: Pressurized shipyards represent the most technologically sophisticated class of orbital repair and construction facilities in the Inner Sphere, providing fully enclosed, atmosphere-controlled working environments that allow construction and maintenance crews to operate without spacesuits. This capability dramatically improves the speed and quality of work compared to the spacesuit-constrained operations required in unpressurized facilities, but at a substantial cost premium that makes pressurized yards far less common than their unpressurized counterparts. Available in configurations ranging from compact single-bay platforms serving low-traffic systems to massive multi-collar installations capable of handling JumpShips and small WarShips, pressurized yards are typically found within larger orbital complexes that include supporting factory stations, habitat platforms, and cargo handling facilities.
fluff.capabilities:
The defining feature of a pressurized yard is the enclosed naval repair facility, which maintains a breathable atmosphere throughout the working volume. This shirt-sleeve environment allows crews to perform fine fabrication, electronics work, and structural repairs that would be significantly more difficult in a spacesuit - translating directly into higher-quality outputs and faster turnaround times compared to equivalent unpressurized operations. Docking collars adjacent to the repair bay allow additional vessels to queue for service, while small craft bays support the continuous movement of personnel and material between the yard and client vessels awaiting entry.

Grav decks housed within the station proper provide crew habitability during extended repair cycles. The station carries no offensive armament in any configuration, relying on the strategic value of functional repair infrastructure and the general prohibition against targeting shipyards to discourage attack. A marine complement provides internal security for visiting vessel crews and protection of the facility's critical systems. The repair bay capacity of each configuration is the primary operational differentiator, ranging from platforms sized for DropShip servicing to installations capable of accommodating the largest JumpShip and WarShip classes.
fluff.deployment: The Pressurized Yard Huge (2450), at 250,000 tons displacement, represents the upper limit of the standardized pressurized yard configurations, capable of servicing JumpShips and small WarShips within a fully enclosed pressurized environment. Four docking collars, twenty small craft bays, accommodations for 1,000 passengers, and an 84-marine security detachment reflect the scale and operational tempo of a facility handling the largest vessel classes. Two large grav decks support extended crew rotations. Installations of this size were found only at the Inner Sphere's most strategically significant star systems during the Star League era, and intact survivors are among the rarest and most valuable orbital assets in existence.
fluff.history:
Pressurized shipyards trace their origins to the early colonization period, when the need to construct and maintain vessels at remote locations (where planetary facilities were unavailable) drove the development of self-contained orbital repair platforms. Early pressurized configurations were crude affairs, but successive generations of construction refined the design into the standardized form documented during the Star League era. The Star League brought systematic expansion of pressurized yard infrastructure across the Inner Sphere, with facilities scaling from compact single-bay platforms at secondary worlds to massive multi-collar installations at major JumpShip and DropShip maintenance hubs.

Unlike factory stations and habitats, pressurized yards demonstrated considerable resilience through the Succession Wars. The progressive destruction of the Inner Sphere's orbital infrastructure made any surviving repair facility extremely valuable, and both formal prohibitions and practical self-interest discouraged belligerents from destroying facilities they might soon need themselves. This unwritten rule (not always honored but widely observed) allowed a significant proportion of pressurized yards to survive through the Succession War period, though many operated at degraded capacity with aging equipment and declining technical staff. The few functioning pressurized yards that maintained full operational capability through the Third Succession War became critical strategic assets, contested by multiple factions and defended at significant cost.

The Clan Invasion and subsequent ilClan period brought renewed demand for shipyard capacity as WarShip production programs resumed and the Inner Sphere's naval ambitions expanded beyond what existing facilities could easily support. Surviving pressurized yards that had maintained functionality found themselves in high demand, while new construction programs began filling critical capability gaps. The majority of pressurized yards operating in the thirty-second century either trace their origins to Star League-era construction or represent post-Clan Invasion new builds, with the smaller configurations proving the most practical targets for new construction given available manufacturing resources.
